entries.message: {where}: {segment} — the position must be {min} to {max}% or a length in vh, vw, px or rem.
{where}: {segment} — {key} does not take {unit}.
entries.fix: It takes {takes}.

entries.message: {where}: {segment} is not a value this property can use.
{where}: {segment} is not a usable band.
a `-{band}` key suffix is no longer read — write the band in the value instead.
entries.fix: keyframes: { {property}: '…; [{band}]: …' }

entries.message: an author rule outranks the generated CSS: computed {property} is {got}, not this element's generated value — the animation sits still and the cascade is doing exactly what CSS does.
entries.fix: Find the winning rule in devtools (the generated selectors are 0-2-0, doubled on purpose); lower its specificity, drop the !important, or scope it away from [data-vm-motion] elements.

entries.message: {where}: two keyframes at {position} — the later one is used.
entries.fix: Either a position is written twice, or a positionless stop landed on an explicit 100%. An ALL-positionless list spreads evenly instead, so give every stop a position or none.

entries.message: wireFunctions: '{name}' is {kind}, not a function or a { run, setup } module; ignoring it.
wireFunctions: '{name}' is already registered; the first registration wins.
entries.fix: Rename one of them — a silent override would leave one module believing its function runs.

entries.message: function '{name}' threw and is disabled for this element. {error}
function: '{name}' names no registered function.
entries.fix: Register it from page code, before elements activate: wireFunctions({ {name}: (el, p) => { … } }).

entries.message: the "when: '{when}'" gate flipped five times in ~a second — a feedback loop (usually: the animation moves the element across its own sensor line). Held at the last state until it settles.
entries.fix: Sense an untransformed wrapper instead of the animated element, or move the trigger line outside the element's own travel.

entries.message: inertia-ease does nothing at inertia: 0 — it shapes the catch-up, and 0 means the values track scroll exactly with no transition to shape.
entries.fix: Raise inertia, or use ease.

entries.message: this value has no CSS spelling: a composite target (transform or filter) whose properties misalign under one non-linear ease, or a third-party discrete hold.
entries.fix: Give each property its own ease (or align the stops), and CSS carries it.

entries.message: motion: keyframes takes an object of properties.
entries.fix: Write keyframes: { opacity: '0% 0, 100% 1' }.

entries.message: {where}: {first} and {used} in one animation; {used} is used throughout.
a wired module threw in {point}; the rest of the chain still ran.
{where}: the nested form needs frames.
entries.fix: Like { frames: '0% 0, 100% 1', ease: 'ease-in' }.

entries.message: {where}: not part of the nested form.
{where}: no keyframes.
{where}: no such key.
entries.fix: Did you mean {meant}?

entries.message: motion: no value — name a preset or write an object.
wiring was given something that is not a vocabulary module: {given}
motion is on a <{tag}>, which this library cannot measure — it reads offsetTop and offsetHeight, which only HTML elements have.
entries.fix: Animate a wrapper around it instead.

entries.message: motion: the braced form must be an object of keys.
{where}: {segment} — {key} takes {low} to {high}.
{where}: "{key}" belongs to the {pack} pack, which is not wired.
entries.fix: Wire it: wireDirectives([motion, {pack}]).

entries.message: motion: could not parse — {detail}.
entries.fix: If a value is text (keyframes, lengths, easings) it has to be quoted.

entries.message: {where}: {segment} — {value} is past the bound this library writes; values stop at {bound}.
path needs path-selector — offset-distance travels along nothing without it.
path-selector '{selector}' {why}
entries.fix: path does nothing.

entries.message: perspective: "{perspective}" is not a length CSS will take — it must not be negative or a percentage.
entries.fix: An invalid perspective() drops the whole transform, so nothing on this element would animate.

entries.message: play and inertia name the same transition, so only one of them can be in force.
entries.fix: Keep play for a timed playthrough, or inertia for a smoothed scrub.

entries.message: the pointer chain lists "{source}" twice.
entries.fix: Each source may appear once — first-available-wins needs no repeats.

entries.message: "rest" is not a chain entry — it is every chain's implicit floor.
entries.fix: Remove it; when nothing is available, the first source's rest value holds.

entries.message: "scroll" leads the chain, and scroll is always available — nothing after it can ever drive.
entries.fix: Put the pointer source first: pointer: 'x, scroll'.

entries.message: after "scroll", {tail} can never drive — scroll is always available.
`pointer` and the `scroll` setting are two competing drivers.
entries.fix: Compose them as a chain instead: pointer: 'x, scroll'.

entries.message: `stagger` does not compose with a pointer source yet (deferred from v1).
{where}: a preset pack failed while resolving "{text}".
entries.fix: The pack is at fault, not the name — the other wired packs were still asked.

entries.message: {where}: "{text}" is not a preset any wired pack knows.
entries.fix: Presets are a pack, so this list is whatever you wired — check that one, not a built-in list.

entries.message: {where}: "{text}" needs a preset pack, and none is wired.
entries.fix: Wire one: wireDirectives([motion, presets]) — or your own.

entries.message: {name} is already registered with a different type, so progress written to it will not interpolate — a play on this element snaps instead of easing.
entries.fix: Pick an unregistered name in progress:, or align your own @property registration to <number>.

entries.message: {key} is a property, and properties are written inside keyframes.
entries.fix: Move it: keyframes: { {key}: … }. The top level holds settings — ease, anchor, scroll, play.

entries.message: wiring was given the property "{key}" with no cssProperty, cssFunction or apply, so it has no way to write anything.
{where}: quote the value — keyframe strings are text.
a re-measure produced no rules for this element; keeping the previous ones.
entries.fix: This should be unreachable — please report the value that did this.

entries.message: two different animations derived the same rule name ({name}), so the second was not applied
entries.fix: a rule name is the hash of the CSS it names, so this should be unreachable — please report it.

entries.message: {where}: {segment} — an unbracketed segment is the base, and there is already one.
frame needs a <canvas> element.
entries.fix: Put the sequence on a <canvas>: it draws each frame into one.

entries.message: this canvas has no 2D context.
entries.fix: A canvas already given another context (webgl, bitmaprenderer) cannot give a 2D one — give the sequence its own <canvas>.

entries.message: frame-count must be a positive number — got "{count}".
entries.fix: Write the number of frames in the sequence: frame-count: 120.

entries.message: frame-url: nothing loaded, starting with {failed}.
entries.fix: frame-url is a PREFIX — check it ends with the folder's slash, and that the first frame exists there.

entries.message: sequence allowedOrigins entry {entry} is not a url; ignoring it.
entries.fix: Write the full origin, for example "https://cdn.example".

entries.message: sequence allowedOrigins must be a list, not {kind}; ignoring it.
entries.fix: Write one origin as a list of one, for example ["https://cdn.example"].

entries.message: frame-url "{url}" is missing or not permitted.
entries.fix: Give a same-origin frame-url, or allow its origin where the module is wired: sequence({ allowedOrigins: [...] }).

entries.message: {where}: is not "<edge> <viewport position>".
entries.fix: One token means the leading edge: '70%' is 'start 70%'.

entries.message: wiring was given "{key}" with both a type and a category.
entries.fix: A setting declares a type and a property declares a category; one descriptor cannot be both.

entries.message: {where}: must be true or false.
{where}: is not an easing name or a cubic-bezier().
{where}: is not a registered function's NAME — bare identifier, no parentheses, never code.
{key} is a setting, and settings are written outside keyframes.
entries.fix: Move it up one level, beside keyframes rather than inside it.

entries.message: {where}: is not a length — use px, rem, em, %, vh or vw.
{where}: was refused by the module that owns it.
{where}: a setting takes a plain value.
{where}: must be a number{range}.
{where}: is not a length or a percentage.
{where}: is not a transform-origin.
{where}: must be a positive length — zero and negatives are invalid CSS, and an invalid perspective() silently kills the whole transform.
pointer takes 'x', 'y' or 'distance', optionally chained with a trailing 'scroll' — like pointer: 'x, scroll'.
{where}: is not a custom property name (--like-this).
{where}: is not one or two comma-separated positions.
entries.fix: scroll: '70%, 50%' scrubs between them; with play: they are the in and out thresholds.

entries.message: {where}: is not a selector this library will use — :has() and a few others are refused.
stagger needs animated descendants — it goes on the parent.
{where}: more than {cap} bands.
{where}: more than {cap} keyframes.
required APIs unavailable, animation disabled.
{where}: not a value this key can use.
a module factory threw while wiring: {detail}
wiring replaced the "{key}" {kind}, which was already registered.
entries.fix: The earlier one is gone, for every element on the page.

entries.message: when: "{when}" uses {blind}, which this library cannot be told about — it re-reads a selector when an attribute changes, and that state is not an attribute.
entries.fix: Use CSS for it. This element animates on scroll instead.
